subject: Future Tech
title: Inside a Quantum Lab
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Inside a Quantum Lab.

hook.text: A quantum computer looks nothing like a laptop. It hangs from the ceiling inside a gold chandelier of wires.

buildup.text: That chandelier is a dilution refrigerator. It cools qubits to near absolute zero, colder than outer space.

discovery.text: The chip itself is tiny, about the size of a thumbnail. Everything else exists to keep it cold and quiet.

twist.text: You can't walk up and type on it. All commands travel as microwave pulses through cables from a control room.

climax.text: These machines cost millions and need dedicated teams, yet cloud access lets anyone run experiments remotely.

punchline.text: The future of computing lives in a freezer.

quiz.question: Why must quantum computers be kept extremely cold?
